summary: Two players each command a deck representing their squads, playing cards to move, spot, suppress, or attack across a hex battlefield inspired by real WWII skirmishes in North Africa. As units take casualties their cards leave the deck (or go into a wound pile), so your options visibly degrade over the course of a scenario, mirroring the attrition of the fight.
praised: elegant fusion of deckbuilding with a tactical wargame
quick to teach despite deep tactics
criticised: card draw luck can swing a scenario
later campaign missions can feel unbalanced
deck thinning can snowball for the player already ahead

interaction.kind: tactical combat on a shared battlefield
interaction.detail: Two players maneuver their own units on one shared hex map, using line of sight and positioning to block routes and set up attacks. Combat directly removes enemy units from the board and can even remove cards from an opponent's deck, so nearly all meaningful state is shared or directly contested rather than private.

subsystems: objective/VP-token control on the map (scenario-specific victory conditions)
sources: VP tokens earned each round for controlling objective hexes
scenario-specific bonus objectives (e.g. eliminating key units, exiting units off-board)
scoring.how_you_win: Play command cards to activate and move/attack with your units, holding more objective hexes than your opponent to rack up VP faster and hit the scenario's VP threshold first (or fulfill the mission's special win condition) before your deck is worn down by casualties.
